name: Grinding, gravity, leaching and Merrill-Crowe precipitation (one milling day)
summary: Every day the mill grinds 600 to 800 tonnes of crushed ore in two ball mills, catches coarse gold in a gravity concentrator and shaking table, and dissolves the rest with cyanide over a day and a half in six leach tanks. The gold-bearing solution is filtered off, clarified, stripped of oxygen and precipitated on zinc dust in sock presses, while the washed solids go to the tailings filters. Four crews on 12-hour shifts run the plant from a control room, and the metallurgist sets daily targets from assays that arrive a day late. Recovery suffers when grind, cyanide, pH or clarity drift, when open pit ore replaces underground ore, or when pumps, filters or power fail, and availability was only 80 to 87% in 2020-2021.

baseline.org_archetype: A single-mine Canadian underground gold producer with a 1,000 to 1,200 tpd gravity and Merrill-Crowe mill running at 460 to 780 tpd, four rotating mill crews and a two-person metallurgy group.
baseline.notes: One case is one 24-hour milling day plus the next morning's review and report. Steps that run in parallel through the day are listed in sequence and marked with concurrent_with.

trigger: The day shift takes over the mill at shift change with crushed ore in the fine ore bin.
end_state: The day's ore has been ground, leached and filtered, the solution has passed through the Merrill-Crowe circuit with gold collecting in the sock press, washed solids have gone to the tailings filters, and the daily report has been sent.

volume.seasonality: Constant: the mill runs every day except during planned shutdowns, such as the August 2021 shutdown that replaced the cone crusher and trash screen. Spring and winter bring more power and feed interruptions but not fewer days.

evidence.note: One case per calendar day; 168,809 t milled in 2019, 236,297 t (646 tpd) in 2020 and 265,267 t (727 tpd) in 2021.

roles.title: Mill process and control room operator

evidence.note: 16 operators in four crews (organisation file), two crews on site on 12-hour day and night shifts (er2016 reports seven-in, seven-out); about 60% of their time on grinding, gravity, leach and Merrill-Crowe, the rest on tailings filters, reagents, water and crushing support.
Four supervisors, one per crew; about 60% of their time on this process.
Two metallurgists on rotation, one on site at a time; targets and the daily report take most of a day shift.
Morning meeting, stops and plan changes.

systems.name: Mill distributed control system and process historian
Shift reports, line-up boards and production tallies (paper and spreadsheets)
Maintenance management system (ERP maintenance module or standalone)
Leaky feeder radio and surface radio network
Incident, inspection and training records system
Gate access, camp booking and gold room access logs
Payroll and timekeeping service (outsourced payroll with site time entry)

resources.name: Crushing-to-precipitation mill (grinding, gravity, leach, Merrill-Crowe, tailings filters)

steps.name: Hold the pre-shift line-up
steps.description: At each shift change the mill shift supervisor meets the incoming crew, reads the previous shift's report, assigns the control room, grinding-leach floor, Merrill-Crowe and tailings filter posts, and gives a short safety talk on lockouts and cyanide work planned. Touch time is the supervisor's time for both shifts of the day.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

control.basis: Pre-shift safety talk and job assignment by a competent supervisor (OHSA supervisor duties; company mill safety procedure)

evidence.note: The reference mill runs 24 hours a day, seven days a week with 12-hour shifts on a seven-in, seven-out rotation (er2016); line-up length is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Take over the control room
steps.description: The incoming control room operator sits with the outgoing operator at the DCS, goes through mill feed tonnage, cyclone pressure, thickener underflow density, leach pH and cyanide, clarifier and press pressures, open alarms and equipment out of service, and signs the handover page. Touch time covers both handovers.

error.defect_description: An open alarm or a bypassed interlock is not passed on.

evidence.note: Central control operators monitor process conditions and keep the shift log (NOC 9231); handover length is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Walk down the wet plant
steps.description: The floor operator walks the two ball mills, cyclones, gravity concentrator, trash screen, thickener, six leach tanks, drum filters and pump floor, checking bearings, oil levels, pump glands, agitators, air sparging and spillage, and radios anything abnormal to the control room. Both shifts make this round.

error.defect_description: A leaking pump gland or hot bearing is missed until it fails.

evidence.note: Equipment list from the reference mill's flowsheet (er2022 section 17.3); round frequency and duration are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Review assays and set the day's targets
steps.description: When the previous day's shift samples are assayed (head, leach feed and tail solution, tails solids, barren solution), the metallurgist opens the results, compares calculated gravity, leach and overall recovery with target, checks the ore blend and sets the day's feed rate, grind, cyanide, lime and zinc targets.

error.defect_description: A setpoint is based on a mislabelled or late sample.

next.condition: assays late or a sample missing

evidence.note: Reference mill recovery 43% gravity, 88% Merrill-Crowe and 97% overall in 2021-22, with a mill laboratory for bench tests (er2022). Overnight assay turnaround and review time are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Chase late assays from the lab
steps.description: The metallurgist phones or walks to the assay lab supervisor to find out why process results are missing, agrees which samples to run first, and decides whether to keep yesterday's setpoints until the numbers arrive.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

evidence.note: Underground grade control samples compete with mill samples in the site lab; the 10% share is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Enter setpoints in the DCS
steps.description: The control room operator types the new mill feed rate, cyclone pressure, cyanide and lime addition and zinc feeder rate into the DCS and notes each change and its reason on the shift log so the next crew knows why the plant moved.

error.defect_description: A setpoint is mistyped, for example cyanide addition by a factor of ten.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of a routine DCS change.

steps.name: Run grinding, thickening, leaching and precipitation from the DCS
steps.description: Across both shifts the control room operator watches mill power and feed tonnage, cyclone density, thickener underflow density and overflow clarity, leach pH and dissolved oxygen, drum filter vacuum, clarifier and sock press pressures and vacuum tower level, and adjusts feed, water and reagent pumps to hold targets. Touch time counts active control minutes; the operator is in the room all day.
outputs: leached pulp to the tailings filters
gold precipitate building in the sock press

error.defect_description: Grind coarsens, cyanide runs low or the thickener overflow turns dirty for hours, and recovery drops.

evidence.note: Two ball mills, pre-leach thickener, six air-sparged leach tanks with 36-38 h retention and a Merrill-Crowe circuit (er2022); mill availability 80.0% in 2020 and 87.3% in 2021 (mda2021). Active control minutes are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Take shift samples and run on-shift titrations
steps.description: Every two to four hours the floor operator cuts samples of cyclone overflow, leach feed and leach discharge, reads pulp density and screen size, titrates free cyanide with silver nitrate, reads pH and dissolved oxygen, and writes the values on the sample board for the control room.

error.defect_description: A sample is mislabelled or a titration end point misread.

control.basis: Cyanide handling procedure: leach pH held at 10.5 to 11.2, PPE and personal HCN monitor worn when sampling

evidence.note: Leach pH 10.5-11.2 and cyanide 0.40-0.57 g/L at the reference mill (er2022); pH above 10.5 prevents hydrogen cyanide (wikicyan). Sample frequency is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Register and deliver samples to the assay lab
steps.description: The operator labels the composite shift sample bags, enters the sample numbers on the lab submission sheet and drives or carries them to the assay lab drop-off before the lab's morning batch cut-off.

error.defect_description: Sample number on the bag does not match the submission sheet.

evidence.note: Author's estimate; the organisation file routes process samples from this process to mill-assay-lab.

steps.name: Dose reagents and check the reagent tanks
steps.description: The utility operator checks the cyanide, lime slurry, flocculant and sodium permanganate day tanks, adjusts dosing pumps to the setpoints, logs tank levels and calls for a new cyanide or flocculant mix when a tank is low. Cyanide mixing needs two trained people and full PPE.

error.defect_description: Dosing pump left at the wrong stroke after a check.

control.basis: Cyanide handling procedure and International Cyanide Management Code practice for mixing and dosing; two-person rule for cyanide mixing

evidence.note: Reagents and 2021 consumption (sodium cyanide 0.52 kg/t, lime 0.79 kg/t, flocculant, permanganate) from er2022; cyanide mixing ventilation at the mill (ero1400). Times are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Run the gravity concentrator and shaking table
steps.description: After each semi-batch cycle of the centrifugal concentrator the operator flushes concentrate to the locked hopper; once a day, with a security officer present, the concentrate is upgraded on the shaking table and the table concentrate is locked in a canister and carried to the refinery vault, both signing the transfer sheet.

error.defect_description: Table tails run high when the deck is set wrongly, sending gold back to the mill.

control.basis: Gold security procedure: two-person custody of gravity and table concentrate, never left unattended

evidence.note: Semi-batch centrifugal concentrator on cyclone feed with daily shaking table upgrade, 43% of gold recovered by gravity (er2022); gravity concentrate never left unattended (goldroom911). The wait for a security escort is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Precoat and change over the clarifiers
steps.description: When a clarifier's pressure rises or the clear solution turns cloudy, the Merrill-Crowe operator takes it offline, washes the leaves, precoats them with Dicalite and Solka Floc slurry and brings it back on line, switching flow to the standby clarifier meanwhile.

error.defect_description: Precoat uneven, letting solids through to the zinc press and lowering precipitate grade.

evidence.note: Three clarifiers (two running, one standby) precoated with Dicalite and Solka Floc; Dicalite 0.19 kg/t (er2022); dicalite vent bin at the mill (ero1400). Frequency is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Check the vacuum tower and zinc feed
steps.description: The operator checks the vacuum towers are pulling the dissolved oxygen out of the clear solution, refills the zinc dust feeder and lead nitrate tank, checks the feeder rate against the setpoint and reads the sock press pressure to judge how full the press is.

error.defect_description: Zinc feeder blocks or vacuum drops and gold stays in barren solution.

next.condition: drum filter cloths need an acid wash

evidence.note: Vacuum towers, zinc dust with lead nitrate, sock presses (er2022); zinc dust 0.086 kg/t. Times are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Acid wash the leach drum filter cloths
steps.description: When filter cake moisture rises or cloths scale up, the operator stops one drum filter, washes the cloth with dilute hydrochloric acid and water, checks the cloth for tears and restarts it, with the other filter carrying the flow.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

control.basis: Lockout and tagging before work on machinery (Ontario Regulation 854 under the OHSA; site lockout procedure)

evidence.note: Two drum filters on leach discharge; hydrochloric acid used for drum filter cleaning and scale removal (er2022). Frequency is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Respond to alarms and process upsets
steps.description: The control room operator acknowledges alarms such as a high mill sump, cyclone roping, a pump trip, a thickener torque alarm or low pH, decides whether to cut feed, change water or start a standby pump, and calls the floor operator to look at the equipment.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

next.condition: upsets handled from the control room
power dip, mill trip or loss of crusher feed

evidence.note: Mill availability was only 80.0% in 2020 and 87.3% in 2021 (mda2021). Split of faults and stops is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Check the fault in the field and isolate the equipment
steps.description: The floor operator goes to the failed pump, screen, agitator or filter, confirms the fault, switches to the standby unit where there is one, and applies a personal lock and tag at the motor control centre so maintenance can work on it safely.

error.defect_description: Wrong isolation point locked; caught at the maintenance try-start.

control.basis: Lockout and tagging before work on machinery (Ontario Regulation 854 under the OHSA; site lockout procedure)

evidence.note: Lockout before maintenance is a legal requirement in Ontario mining plants; the regulation text could not be opened, so the basis is general knowledge.

steps.name: Make a controlled mill stop and notify the superintendent
steps.description: After a power dip, a mill trip or a long crusher stoppage, the shift supervisor decides whether to stop the ball mills, keeps leach agitators, air and the thickener rake running, and phones the mill superintendent and the power utility or crusher operator to find out how long the stop will last.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

next.condition: no repair needed, wait for power or feed

evidence.note: Six milling days lost to cone crusher downtime in December 2020 (wes2020); the mill is on a 70 km power line from Wawa with diesel backup that cannot sustain production (er2016). Frequency is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Raise a work request with maintenance
steps.description: The shift supervisor radios the maintenance supervisor, then types a work request in the maintenance system with the equipment number, fault and priority, so a millwright or electrician is sent and the job is recorded.

error.defect_description: Vague fault description sends the wrong trade first.

evidence.note: Author's estimate; work requests go to mnt-breakdown-repair in the organisation file.

steps.name: Restart the circuit after the repair
steps.description: Once the millwright or electrician signs off and removes their locks, the floor operator removes the personal lock, try-starts the equipment, and the control room brings feed back up in steps while watching mill power, sump levels and thickener torque.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

evidence.note: Wait is the time to get a trade and finish the repair; repair labour is counted in mnt-breakdown-repair.

steps.name: Inspect the mill as shift supervisor
steps.description: The shift supervisor walks the mill once a shift, checks housekeeping, guards, eyewash stations and fixed HCN monitors, talks to each operator, and records the inspection and any hazards in the inspection record.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

control.basis: Supervisor workplace inspections under the Occupational Health and Safety Act and Regulation 854 (mines and mining plants)

evidence.note: Supervisor inspection duties under Ontario law; the regulation text could not be opened, so frequency and duration are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Record the shift log
steps.description: Near the end of each shift the control room operator fills in the shift log: tonnes from the mill feed weightometer, mill running hours, reagent and zinc use from tank dips, downtime with cause codes and sample times, partly copied from the DCS historian into the shift spreadsheet.

error.defect_description: Downtime coded to the wrong cause or tonnes copied from the wrong totaliser.

evidence.note: Weightometer on the second mill feed conveyor (er2022); control operators keep the shift log (NOC 9231). Time is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Review the shift report and timesheets
steps.description: The shift supervisor checks the shift log against what happened, adds notes on safety, delays and work requests, approves crew hours in the timekeeping sheet and saves the report before handing over.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

evidence.note: Author's estimate; the organisation file sends timesheets from this process to site-payroll.

steps.name: Review the milling day at the morning meeting
steps.description: At the morning production meeting the mill superintendent goes through tonnes milled, availability, estimated head grade and recovery, reagent use and open work orders with the metallurgist and shift supervisor, and decides on changes such as a lower feed rate for hard ore.

error.defect_description: None introduced; errors pass through.

next.condition: blend, grind or reagent plan changed

evidence.note: A daily production meeting is common practice at Canadian mines; timing and change rate are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Revise the blend, grind or reagent plan
steps.description: The metallurgist works out new targets, for example more cyanide and a slower feed for Mishi open pit ore, which bypasses the gravity circuit and recovers less, writes them on the setpoint sheet and tells the crusher operator and shift supervisor.

error.defect_description: Change not passed to the night crew.

evidence.note: Gravity is used only for Eagle ore, and Mishi ore recovers 83% overall against 97% (er2022); Mishi recovery 77.8% in 2020 (wes2020). Change frequency is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Send the daily mill report
steps.description: The metallurgist copies the day's tonnes, availability, estimated grade, recovery and reagent use into the daily report workbook and emails it to the general manager, mine superintendent and the metallurgical accounting file.

error.defect_description: A number is copied wrongly; corrected at month-end reconciliation.

evidence.note: Author's estimate; the shift log and daily balance feed mill-met-accounting.

exceptions.name: Equipment fault needing maintenance
exceptions.description: A pump, screen, agitator or filter fails; the operator isolates it, the supervisor raises a work request and the circuit restarts after the repair.

exceptions.name: Mill stop after a power dip or loss of crusher feed
exceptions.description: The supervisor makes a controlled stop and waits for power, crusher repair or maintenance before restarting.

exceptions.name: Late assays
exceptions.description: The lab has not released process results and the metallurgist chases them, holding yesterday's setpoints.

exceptions.name: Drum filter acid wash
exceptions.description: A leach drum filter is stopped for an acid wash and cloth check.

exceptions.name: Ore change needs new targets
exceptions.description: A new stope or open pit stockpile blend arrives and the metallurgist revises grind, feed and reagent targets.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from day-shift takeover to the daily report the next morning
benchmarks.population: One milling day at a single-line gold mill

evidence.note: A milling day lasts 24 hours by definition and the report follows the next morning. The simulator adds parallel steps in sequence, so its cycle time is longer; see assumptions.
Mishi open pit ore: no gravity, 94% Merrill-Crowe, 83% overall.
Planning basis 93.3% (er2022).

pain_points.description: Assays come back the next morning, so the plant runs a full day on titrations and yesterday's numbers before a grade or recovery problem shows.

evidence.note: Overnight fire assay turnaround for process samples is the author's estimate.

pain_points.description: Equipment faults force lockouts, a maintenance call and a stepwise restart; mill availability was 80% in 2020 and 87% in 2021 against a 93% plan.
Clarifier precoats, zinc feed and drum filter washes need constant attention; a dirty or oxygenated solution leaves gold in the barren solution.

evidence.note: Merrill-Crowe circuit design and the planned cyanide analyser (er2022); the effect on losses is the author's reading.

pain_points.description: Shift logs are copied by hand from the DCS into spreadsheets, and wrong downtime codes or totaliser readings surface only at month-end reconciliation.

evidence.note: Spreadsheet shift reports are listed as a system in the organisation file; error rate is the author's estimate.

pain_points.description: Open pit ore bypasses the gravity circuit and recovers much less, so blend changes need new targets.

sources.title: Technical Report for the Eagle River Gold Mining Complex, Ontario, Canada (NI 43-101, SRK Consulting, 22 April 2022)
sources.supports: Section 17: mill permitted to 1,200 t/d on a crushing basis; three stockpile pads; loader feeds the jaw crusher, cone in closed circuit with a double-deck screen, fine ore bin, weightometer on the second mill feed conveyor; crushing product 80% passing 9/16 inch; primary and secondary ball mills with cyclones, 75% passing 74 um; semi-batch centrifugal gravity concentrator on cyclone feed, shaking table daily and magnetic separation; trash screen, pre-leach thickener (permanganate, flocculant, cyanide); six leach tanks (one standby), air sparged, 36-38 h retention, pH 10.5-11.2; drum filters; three clarifiers precoated with Dicalite and Solka Floc; vacuum towers, zinc dust and lead nitrate, sock presses with socks removed bi-weekly; tailings filtered on drum filters and conveyed for dry stacking; refinery with CCTV, vault, sock burner oven and propane Wabi furnace smelting table concentrate and burned sock ash to doré of 80-94% gold; hydrogen peroxide cyanide destruction in the Reclaim Pond; 2021-22 mill availability basis 93.3% (86% in 2021), average 779 t/d; recovery gravity 43%, Merrill-Crowe 88%, overall 97%; reagent use (NaCN 0.52 kg/t, lime 0.79 kg/t, zinc 0.086 kg/t). Sections 18.7 and 20.3: filtered tailings conveyed to stockpiles and redistributed by trucks and a dozer; Reclaim Pond feeds the mill; excess water treated to the Polishing Pond or stored in the Mishi pit; dam raises 2019 (Stage 3), 2020 (Stage 4) and 2022-24 (Stage 5); annual Dam Safety Inspections by consultants (SNC-Lavalin 2020, EXP 2021) under CDA guidelines, the Lakes and Rivers Improvement Act and MAC guidance; dams classed High; mill 17 km by road from the mine

sources.title: Technical Report for the Eagle River Mining Complex (NI 43-101, G. Mannard and P. Ng, 17 March 2016)
sources.supports: Section 17: mill 17 km by road from the mine; Merrill-Crowe zinc precipitation with about 40% of gold to a Knelson gravity concentrate; precipitate refined on site to doré of 80-92% gold shipped to the Royal Canadian Mint; recovery about 95%; reclaim water reused; the mill runs 24 hours a day, seven days a week with crews on 12-hour shifts on a seven days in, seven days out rotation; practical limit about 1,050 t/d because of maintenance time

sources.title: Wesdome Gold Mines Ltd. 2021 annual management's discussion and analysis

sources.title: Wesdome Announces 2020 Fourth Quarter and Full Year Production Results; Provides 2021 Guidance
sources.publisher: Wesdome Gold Mines Ltd. (news release, via Yahoo Finance)
sources.supports: Ore milled 2019 (168,809 t) and 2020 (236,297 t) including Mishi open pit ore; Eagle River recovery 97.7% and Mishi recovery 77.8% in 2020; gold produced 91,688 oz (2019) and 90,278 oz (2020); six days of milling lost in December 2020 to mechanical downtime on the cone crusher; Mishi stockpile of over 40,000 t to be milled in 2021

sources.title: Wesdome Gold Mines Ltd. - Environmental Compliance Approval (air), Eagle River Mill (ERO 012-8749)
sources.supports: Amended air approval of 21 December 2020 for the Eagle River Mill, 50 km west of Wawa: replacement of the laboratory fume hood and bullion furnace, a dicalite vent bin collection system, hydrogen cyanide emissions from the tailings pond and leach tanks, cyanide building and cyanide mixing ventilation; contaminants include hydrogen cyanide and zinc

sources.title: Gold Room Security
sources.supports: Double-locked single entry using card passes; CCTV with 90-day recorder and card access; permanent hardcover gold room book recording date, batch number, weights and conversions; very few people should know of pours or pickups; never leave cathode cake, gravity concentrate or smelted products unattended; insiders are historically the greatest threat; monthly metallurgical reconciliation highlights larger thefts

sources.title: Gold cyanidation
sources.supports: Lime or soda keeps leach pH above 10.5 to prevent hydrogen cyanide; oxygen deficiency slows leaching; carbon in pulp is the most economical recovery method; SO2/air cyanide destruction adds sodium metabisulfite and air with lime near pH 8.5 and copper sulfate catalyst

sources.title: Explore subgroup: 9231 Central control and process operators, mineral and metal processing
sources.publisher: Employment and Social Development Canada, National Occupational Classification
sources.supports: Unit group operates and monitors multi-function process control machinery to control the processing of mineral ores; example titles include central control room operator and chief flotation operator

assumptions: The reference mill recovers gold by gravity concentration and Merrill-Crowe zinc precipitation, not by carbon in pulp (er2022, er2016). The organisation file's process name and its link object 'loaded_carbon' to mill-elution-refining assume carbon; this file keeps the object id because the organisation file has no business object for gold precipitate or table concentrate, and uses it to stand for both.

This daily case covers the continuous wet plant, including the clarifiers, vacuum towers and zinc feed. The batch work of changing sock presses and smelting precipitate and table concentrate is in mill-elution-refining.

touch_min on the long control step (s07) counts active control minutes, not the full 24 hours the operator is in the control room. The steps account for about 30 of roughly 110 crew person-hours a milling day; the rest is standby, housekeeping, breaks and training not tied to a step.

The simulator adds every step in sequence, so its median cycle time (about 1.5 days) is longer than the real 24 hours plus a morning report, in which control, sampling, dosing and Merrill-Crowe work run at the same time (marked with concurrent_with).
Repair labour for equipment faults is counted in mnt-breakdown-repair; here it appears only as the wait before s19.

The mill-plant resource is held 1,100 to 1,440 minutes a day to match 80 to 87% availability in 2020-2021 (mda2021). The organisation file gives it 640 to 710 available hours a month (about 89 to 99%), which is higher than the reference mill achieved, and a running cost of C$900 to C$1,500 an hour (C$22,000 to C$36,000 a day), which is high against a total processing cost of about C$31 per tonne at the neighbouring Island Gold mill (igtr2020 in the organisation file).

Mill crews at the reference mine worked 12-hour shifts on a seven-in, seven-out rotation (er2016), not the 14/14 rotation the organisation file gives the site; the shift_24x7 pattern on the mill roles still fits.
Loaded costs come from the organisation file (wage times 1.35 for hourly site roles, 1.30 for staff).

Organisation file corrected on 2026-11-24 to match this workflow's sources: ids were renamed (mill-elution-refining to mill-gold-room-refining, loaded_carbon to gold_concentrate, tailings_slurry to filtered_tailings, elution-circuit to refinery), and roles and resources this workflow added are now in the organisation file. Notes above that describe a mismatch refer to the file before the correction.
